diagram_math_checks.evidence: Local def-hom-double-complex-of-a-projective-and-an-injective-resolution defines K^{p,q}=Hom(P_p,I^q). Top row is q=0, bottom q=1, left p=0, right p=1. Precomposition with d_{P,1}:P_1→P_0 sends Hom(P_0,I^q) to Hom(P_1,I^q), hence both horizontal arrows point right and have bidegree (1,0).

Postcomposition with d_I^0:I^0→I^1 sends each Hom(P_p,I^0) to Hom(P_p,I^1), so both arrows point down and have bidegree (0,1). Both composites on f:P_0→I^0 equal d_I^0∘f∘d_{P,1}; this is Verification 1.1 and the local commuting-differentials lemma 1.1. The square asserts unsigned commutation, not anticommutation.

Local total-complex definition and Verification 2.1 use D|K^{p,q}=d_h+(-1)^p d_v and finite p+q diagonals. Thus Tot^0=K^{0,0}, Tot^1=K^{1,0}⊕K^{0,1}, Df=(fd_P,d_If). For a:P_1→I^0 and b:P_0→I^1, the mixed K^{1,1} component is -d_Ia+bd_P. Applied to Df it is -d_Ifd_P+d_Ifd_P=0; pure components vanish by the resolution square-zero identities. No full Tot^2 is falsely identified with the single displayed mixed object.
